key_insight: Stoichiometry-preserved ionic clusters, paired with pretrained MLIPs and multi-task fine-tuning, can predict detonation performance of multi-ionic energetic materials before full crystal structures are known.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical pre-synthesis screening route for data-scarce energetic materials, helping prioritize promising compositions without expensive crystal-structure prediction.
method: Represent each candidate as a non-periodic stoichiometric ionic cluster instead of a full periodic crystal.
Start from a pretrained atomistic backbone and fine-tune with an energy-forces multi-task objective as physical regularization.
Use the learned surrogate to screen new ABX4 materials with unseen stoichiometry and cation chemistry.
evidence_signal: On 25 curated perovskite-type energetic materials, the cross-validated surrogate was aligned to experimentally derived Kamlet-Jacobs detonation velocities and achieved 92 m/s MAE on three newly synthesized ABX4 compounds without retraining.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on a small, curated dataset, so broader generalization to more diverse multi-ionic chemistries and less regular structures may require additional validation.
paper_title: Stoichiometric cluster learning for few-shot property prediction of multi-ionic integrated energetic materials
